title: Beam FileShare: Local Wi-Fi File Sharing
description: Share files across local Wi-Fi with Beam FileShare. Host on Windows, macOS, Linux or Android; everyone else uses a browser. No cloud uploads or receiver app.
og_description: Open-source local Wi-Fi file sharing for Windows, Mac, Linux and Android. No cloud storage or receiver app.
hero_eyebrow: Free · open source · local Wi-Fi file sharing
h1: Share files over local Wi-Fi, without cloud uploads.
lead: Beam FileShare runs on one Windows, macOS, Linux, or Android device. Others open its link in a browser to upload or download files on the same trusted network.
hero_note: Transfers use your local network. Use Beam FileShare on a network you trust.
visual_alt: Illustration of a phone and computer sharing a file over a local Wi‑Fi connection
how_title: From first launch to shared files
how_intro: One device hosts the folder. Other devices join from a browser.
step1_text: Run Beam FileShare on the device that will host the shared folder.
step2_text: Connect devices to the same Wi‑Fi, or start a private Beam network.
step3_text: Scan the QR code or type the link on a phone or computer. No receiver app needed.
download_intro: Choose a platform and build type. Beam recommends the closest match for your device above.
download_iphone_text: You do not need to install Beam on the receiving device. Open the shared link in Safari to upload or download files.
feature_local_text: Beam FileShare sends files across your local network instead of uploading them to cloud storage.
feature_receiver_text: Send the link to a phone, tablet, or computer. Recipients do not need an account or Beam installed.
feature_resume_text: Beam sends files in checked chunks and can continue after a connection drop.
feature_open_text: Beam FileShare is MIT-licensed. Review the source and release checksums on GitHub.
trust_text: Beam FileShare is built for local-network sharing. Use it on a network you trust, and share only folders you intend others on that network to access.
faq1_q: Do both devices need Beam FileShare installed?
faq1_a: No. Run Beam FileShare only on the device hosting the shared folder. Other devices join using a web browser.
faq2_q: Does Beam FileShare need internet to transfer files?
faq2_a: File transfers work over a local Wi-Fi network without internet. Internet is needed to download Beam FileShare or check GitHub for a new release.
faq3_a: Choose a build for the device that will run Beam FileShare. Most Windows PCs use x64; most Intel or AMD Linux computers use x64; newer Macs use Apple Silicon. Android uses the APK.
faq4_q: Does Beam FileShare upload files to cloud storage?
faq4_a: No. Beam FileShare transfers files across your local network instead of uploading them to a cloud-storage service.
faq5_q: Can I use Beam FileShare from an iPhone?
faq5_a: Yes. Use Safari to open the host’s shared link as a receiving device. You do not need to install Beam FileShare on the iPhone.
footer: Built for sharing on your local network.
proof_one_text: The Windows, Mac, Linux or Android host
proof_two_text: No Beam FileShare install on other devices
proof_three_text: No cloud storage in the middle
terminal_note: The installer detects your operating system and architecture.
noscript_text: Beam FileShare downloads and product information are available without JavaScript.
checksum_text: Check release files with the published SHA256 checksums.
platform_windows_desc: Choose x64 for most PCs, or ARM64 for ARM-powered devices.
platform_macos_desc: Choose Apple Silicon for M-series Macs, or Intel for older Macs.
platform_linux_desc: Choose a portable build or the package format used by your distribution.
platform_android_desc: Install Beam on the Android device that will host files.
guides_intro: Practical help for sharing files locally, choosing a host, and joining from another device.
guide_wifi_title: Share files over Wi-Fi without cloud uploads
guide_wifi_desc: Set up a local file-sharing host and open it from another device’s browser.
guide_android_title: Transfer files between Android and Windows
guide_android_desc: Use Android or Windows as the host and move files over the same Wi-Fi network.
